question: Which hormone tells the Leydig cells in the testes to produce testosterone?
explanation: Spot on! Luteinizing hormone (LH) comes from the anterior pituitary gland and travels down to tell the Leydig cells to make testosterone. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why do problems in the brain-testicle hormone pathway (hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis) often affect both sperm and testosterone?

options.A: Because the pituitary gland directly manufactures all male gametes
options.B: Because hypothalamic neurons physically transform into mature spermatozoa
options.C: Because testosterone is exclusively stored in the anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Because the axis controls both testosterone production and germ cell maturation

explanation: Think of the brain as the master switch that controls two main factories: Leydig cells for testosterone and Sertoli cells for sperm. When the master switch has issues, both processes are affected! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h1)

question: In benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), which part of the prostate gland usually enlarges first?
explanation: The transition zone wraps tightly around the urethra. That's why when it grows in BPH, it pinches the pipe early and causes those annoying urinary symptoms! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h2)

question: What is the main job of nitric oxide when a man gets an erection?

options.A: Stimulating the sympathetic nervous system to contract the prostate
options.B: Relaxing smooth muscle to allow blood to fill the corpora cavernosa
options.C: Constricting local arteries to trap blood inside the pelvic cavity
options.D: Destroying excess fibrous tissue within the tunica albuginea

explanation: Nitric oxide acts like a smooth muscle relaxant in the blood vessels, letting blood rush in and fill the chambers (corpora cavernosa) to create firmness. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h2)

question: What is the main use of the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) questionnaire?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the prostate gland in grams
options.B: To calculate the total residual urine volume in the bladder
options.C: To quantify the severity of urinary symptoms in patients
options.D: To screen exclusively for metastatic prostate cancer cells

explanation: The IPSS is simply a handy questionnaire used to ask patients how badly their urinary symptoms are bothering them in daily life. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h3)

question: A patient's prostate-specific antigen (PSA) blood test comes back a little high. What should you as a nurse keep in mind?

options.A: It is a definitive confirmation that malignant prostate cancer is present
options.B: It proves the patient has a severe urinary tract infection
options.C: It can be elevated due to benign growth, infection, or recent manipulation
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will require immediate surgical removal

explanation: Remember, PSA is sensitive to lots of things! A simple infection, a routine exam, or just natural aging (BPH) can make PSA go up, not just cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h3)

question: How do alpha-1 blockers help a patient with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)?

options.A: By increasing the systemic production of free testosterone
options.B: By shrinking the total volume of the prostate gland over time
options.C: By relaxing smooth muscle in the prostate and bladder neck
options.D: By directly killing abnormal cells lining the urethral wall

explanation: Alpha-1 blockers relax the tight muscles around the prostate and bladder opening, making it much easier for urine to flow out. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why shouldn't patients take erectile dysfunction drugs like sildenafil (Viagra) together with organic nitrates?

options.A: It causes sudden and permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: It completely stops all normal urine production in the kidneys
options.C: It triggers rapid bone marrow suppression and severe anemia
options.D: It can cause a severe and life-threatening drop in blood pressure

explanation: Both drugs cause blood vessels to open up wide (vasodilation). Combined, they can cause blood pressure to crash to dangerous levels. Always check medication history! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is the main goal of continuous bladder irrigation (CBI) after prostate surgery?

options.A: To deliver strong antibiotic drugs directly to the prostate tissue
options.B: To permanently shrink any remaining benign prostate cells
options.C: To measure the exact daily hormonal output of the testes
options.D: To prevent blood clot retention and keep the catheter open

explanation: After surgery, bleeding can form clots that block the catheter. CBI flushes fluid in and out continuously to keep everything clear and flowing! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h5)

question: During continuous bladder irrigation, which finding means you need to take action right away?

options.A: Mild lower abdominal cramping associated with bladder spasms
options.B: Light pink, clear fluid flowing steadily into the collection bag
options.C: Sudden dark red output with large clots and absent drainage
options.D: Clear yellowish urine mixing slowly with the incoming irrigation fluid

explanation: If fluid is going in but not coming out, and the tubing looks blocked with dark clots, the catheter is obstructed! You need to act fast to prevent bladder damage. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which nursing diagnosis fits best for a patient struggling with painful bladder spasms and trouble urinating due to an enlarged prostate?
explanation: An enlarged prostate blocks the normal flow of urine, directly leading to an alteration in urinary elimination. Perfect match for the nursing care plan! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h6)

question: A patient feels very embarrassed and down about sexual changes after prostate surgery. How should you respond as a nurse?

options.A: Acknowledge his feelings and offer a supportive, nonjudgmental space to discuss concerns
options.B: Tell him that sexual function is entirely unimportant compared to curing his urinary obstruction
options.C: Advise him to immediately stop taking all prescribed postoperative medications
options.D: Assure him that normal function always returns within twenty-four hours

explanation: Being heard and accepted with empathy helps patients cope with sensitive body-image and emotional challenges after major surgery. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the immediate action needed for a patient in acute urinary retention?

options.B: Application of warm compresses to the lower back
options.C: Immediate open surgical removal of the prostate gland
options.D: Urinary catheterization to relieve bladder distension

explanation: When a patient cannot pass urine and is in agonizing pain, the immediate fix is draining the bladder safely with a urinary catheter. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h7)

question: Which signs point toward acute bacterial prostatitis turning into a dangerous systemic infection (urosepsis)?

options.A: Gradual hair loss across the chest and abdomen
options.B: Low resting heart rate and warm, dry skin
options.C: Painless swelling of the bilateral ankle joints
options.D: High fever, rigors, and severe perineal pain

explanation: Look out for red flag infection signs! Severe shaking chills (rigors), high fever, and intense pelvic pain mean the infection is spreading systemically. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h7)

question: What lifestyle tip should you give a patient who keeps waking up all night to urinate (nocturia)?

options.A: Drinking two large glasses of water right before bed
options.B: Increasing consumption of strong caffeinated coffee
options.C: Eliminating all dietary protein from daily meals
options.D: Limiting fluid intake in the evening hours

explanation: A simple trick to reduce nighttime bathroom trips is cutting back on fluids a few hours before bedtime. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h8)

question: Why are pelvic floor (Kegel) exercises suggested for patients recovering from prostate surgery?

options.A: To prevent the development of bacterial infections in the kidneys
options.B: To eliminate the need for any future follow-up clinic visits
options.C: To permanently increase the resting size and blood flow of the prostate
options.D: To strengthen muscles that support urinary control and help reduce incontinence

explanation: Pelvic floor exercises tone up the sphincter muscles, helping patients regain control over their bladder and stop unwanted leakage. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h8)
